issue_plan.name: Tighten native acceptance plumbing
issue_plan.summary: Four sequential plumbing changes cover issue #510: reuse immutable repository facts, centralize acceptance rules and queue authority, render native ratification text safely, and fetch dashboard acceptance sources only when opened. The split keeps snapshot and hash compatibility, validation compatibility, GitHub rendering, and dashboard delivery independently reviewable. Existing ratified hashes, source bytes, execution evidence rules and external-plumbing restrictions remain intact; the intended presentation change removes inline sources from polled dashboard state. Each issue includes its tests and current-state documentation, with any new implementation decision recorded by the merger.

issues.title: Reuse captured repository facts in native acceptance
issues.body:
Issue #510 found that native acceptance recognizes an absent file by comparing an error message, repeats the repository's deepest-owner algorithm, and rereads immutable declared blobs for every execution digest. Complete these related repository and digest changes in one plumbing pull request.

Give a missing regular-file path in a successfully captured repository tree a distinct error that callers can recognize with errors.Is. Keep repository.ErrMissing exclusively for an absent repository contract. Invalid syntax, unsafe ancestors, directories, symbolic links, gitlinks, cancellation and unreadable Git objects must not qualify as absent files. Change ReadRepositoryDraft to use the typed distinction instead of requireFile's message text, retaining its refusal of an acceptance file already present in the captured base.

Expose the deepest enclosing directory owner through repository.Snapshot for existing, new and deleted file paths, with the same path validation and independent returned Part data as the other snapshot queries. A root part is only the fallback; path-component boundaries and nested parts matter. Use this one directory-owner rule in both PartsFor and Plan.repositoryDigest. PartsFor must still add shared-path and dependency-input owners, select all parts for the contract/rules/current-state documents, and reject every unsafe or unowned touched path. Those additional check owners must never let native acceptance execute outside its deepest enclosing part; no directory owner is an error for native acceptance even if a shared rule selects checks.

Reuse successfully read committed blob bytes within each immutable snapshot so repeated execution-digest validation no longer runs Git again for the same inputs. Return independent byte slices, support concurrent readers without races, honor each caller's cancellation even on a cache hit, and do not cache failed or canceled reads as success. Reuse is scoped to the captured authority, never to a moving ref or candidate path. A new snapshot with changed declared input bytes must still change authority. Use the existing dependencyHash helper for the digest's sha256 encoding without changing its versioned canonical JSON, exact byte inputs, sorted sets, argv ordering, exclusions or hash format. Keep captured commit provenance outside the ratified hash; no lock migration or rewrite is permitted.

The relevant production code is internal/repository/{repository.go,snapshot.go,ownership.go} and internal/plumbing/{native.go,dependencies.go}. Before the child plan names writable files, inspect the existing repository tests in contract_accept_test.go, ownership_test.go and snapshot_test.go, and plumbing's native_identity_accept_test.go, native_regression_test.go, native_review_regression_test.go and native_execution_accept_test.go. They pin fresh returned data, nested/root/shared ownership, missing objects, cancellation, unchanged legacy hashes and committed locks, canonical declaration order, and the exclusion of rule/document bytes and other parts' dependencies. Name any existing test the implementation must edit; keep the pinned behaviors.

Add focused acceptance and regression coverage for errors.Is classification, owner-query agreement with native binding, independent returned data, concurrent and canceled cache reads, and repeated digest validation without repeated blob reads. Use deterministic read counting or a controlled Git fixture rather than a timing threshold. Verify changed snapshots still invalidate changed policy/input authority and that equivalent inputs retain exactly the old digest and plan hash. Run affected Go suites and the race detector for the cache tests; no Docker or network is needed for these cases.

Update the repository-contract and native-acceptance detail in docs/factory.md, and the affected repository-contract description in SPEC.md, to describe the new snapshot query, absence error and reuse while preserving authority guarantees. Cite D-0301 and D-0314 on changed SPEC bullets, with D-0105 and D-0122 as applicable. This work rests on D-0301 (captured tree and ownership), D-0314 (content-bound native identity), D-0107 (hash-pinned plans), D-0317 (existing test compatibility) and D-0294 (detail in linked docs). The merger records the new snapshot API/cache decision; the build cannot write decisions/. External plumbing remains disabled under D-0121.

issues.title: Centralize acceptance declarations and retained queue authority
issues.body:
Issue #510 found duplicate Go AST walkers, repeated framework definitions, and duplicate planning-check repository state. After the repository-facts step has merged, complete this internal acceptance refactor in one plumbing pull request, preserving existing admitted and refused behaviors.

Replace the separate AST walks in plumbing.declares and acceptanceDeclarations with one Go declaration analysis used by both callers. Keep the legacy compatibility policy explicit instead of silently imposing new native restrictions on old locks. Native Go must retain its stricter requirements: the selected top-level function occurs exactly once, has no receiver, type parameters or results, and has one *testing.T parameter with the captured testing import, including supported alias and dot imports. Select the top-level function from the exact native selector, never its display label. Keep package-wide ambiguity checks and runtime/discovery evidence separate from this structural analysis. Non-Go sources remain verbatim UTF-8 data for their adapters, never Go-parsed.

Define framework metadata once and consume it for source-language display (including JS versus TS extensions), file/selector structural checks, owning-part language requirements, declaration dispatch and default adapter selection. Cover go, pytest, vitest and jest as the current schema does; keep pytest's part-relative file check and literal Go subtest / JS nested-title semantics. Preserve trusted adapter overrides, existing supported invocation forms and flags, unsupported-invocation refusal before preparation, and the distinction between structural validity and executable support. This is reuse, not an adapter rollout or removal: preserve the execution capabilities already implemented on the base where this issue is taken, and do not change their evidence protocol, deadlines, isolation or cleanup.

Remove checkBuild.repo and use the registered sandbox.Original as the single retained repository path for planning checks. Distinguish planning from building by registration mode/plan presence, not by whether Original is empty: both types can retain an original checkout. A planning registration must still reject build execution, and a build registration must still reject replacement planning requests. Remove the redundant assignment to f.Sandbox.Original in formalize.Plan; RegisterPlan captures the supplied repository for queued checks, and final validation continues to use the same original repository and snapshot. Keep registration copies of plans and adapter maps, child-request authority restrictions, shared allowance and queue-slot ownership through cleanup.

Start with internal/plumbing/{plan.go,native.go,repository_acceptance.go,checkqueue.go} and internal/formalize/plan.go, adding a small shared declaration/framework implementation if needed. Inspect plan_test.go, native_identity_accept_test.go, native_execution_accept_test.go, native_regression_test.go, native_review_regression_test.go, configured_queue_610_accept_test.go, checkqueue_regression_test.go, check_queue_accept_test.go and repository_go_queue_accept_test.go in internal/plumbing, plus native_planning_accept_test.go and configured_go_planner_610_accept_test.go in internal/formalize. The native planning fake extracts -check-queue/-check-build from GateServer and deliberately edits the candidate contract; its opaque native-runner pytest wrapper must remain refused before preparation. Also inspect go_selection_accept_test.go, pytest_selection_617_accept_test.go and node_selection_633_accept_test.go before changing metadata or adapter lookup: their exact argv/flag and selector assertions stay authoritative. Name every existing test that the child build must edit.

Test the new shared declaration/framework API with positive and negative cases and its use by native and legacy plan validation, preserving alias handling, malformed declarations, duplicate names, language/file mismatches, complete native identities, unchanged legacy hashes and committed locks. Exercise planning and build registrations with nonempty Original values, forbidden cross-mode requests, caller mutation after registration, cancellation and cleanup, and agreement between the planning tool and fresh final validation. Add tests for any new reusable API rather than source-text assertions that merely count walkers or fields. Run the affected Go suites with their existing fake runners; retain their command contracts and refusal assertions.

This step rests on D-0105, D-0107 and D-0314 for plan compatibility, D-0301 for captured authority, D-0303 for queue ownership and budgets, D-0311 for configured checks, D-0316 for the acceptance lifecycle, and D-0317 for existing tests and fakes. Keep SPEC.md and docs/factory.md accurate under D-0122/D-0294 if any documented API or description needs adjusting; no change to framework support is authorized by this refactor. The merger records the implementation reuse decision, without editing existing ratified plans or locks. External plumbing stays disabled under D-0121.

issues.title: Keep native ratification text literal on GitHub
issues.body: Issue #510 found that the native acceptance table in a factory ratification comment can turn a display label or assertion containing @user or #123 into a GitHub mention or issue reference. It also found that factory.planText duplicates receipt.componentText. Complete the shared renderer and native-table fix together in one plumbing pull request. Export one reusable literal-text escaping implementation from the existing receipt rendering code and use it for both receipt text and factory proposal text, removing the duplicate escape/autolink implementation. Retain the receipt's current literal rendering, JSON values and legacy receipt compatibility. The shared text encoder must preserve visible text while preventing Markdown/HTML interpretation, table-cell or row breaks, and GFM URL/email autolinks. A text encoder alone is not sufficient protection against GitHub mentions: put native acceptance labels and assertions, along with their existing literal identity fields, in a code/literal context where GitHub does not create user/team mentions or issue/PR references. Handle @user, @org/team, #123 and owner/repository#123 alongside embedded backticks, pipes, backslashes, HTML, entity-looking text, quotes and assertion line endings. Escape exactly once for the chosen context, use safe code delimiters where applicable, and keep the table readable with one row per acceptance record. The complete part/framework/file/selector identity, captured execution digest/base and language-tagged verbatim source blocks must remain visible. Preserve raw labels, assertions and source bytes in the hidden marker, saved proposal and lock, and preserve proposal hashes and the ratification command. This changes native table presentation only; authored explanatory prose and command links keep their behavior. The main production sites are internal/receipt/receipt.go and internal/factory/plancomments.go; inspect other receipt callers before exporting or renaming the helper. Existing tests to inspect include internal/factory/native_proposal_accept_test.go and internal/receipt/{component_markdown_accept_test.go,explicit_literals_accept_test.go,component_sources_accept_test.go}. issues.title: Fetch dashboard acceptance sources by proposal hash
issues.body:
Issue #510 found that /api/state.json sends every waiting plumbing proposal's full acceptance sources on each 15-second poll. Complete a read-only source endpoint and both dashboard-page consumers in one plumbing pull request after the earlier reuse changes have merged.

Keep summary, writable files, trusted files, acceptance assertions, full native identities and execution metadata in the waiting proposal's lightweight state view, but remove all full acceptance-source bodies from the polled JSON. Give that view a source URL keyed by the complete proposal content hash, separate from Waiting.Hash's existing 12-character display/ratification shorthand. Serve the exact source map and language hints for that full hash through a read-only JSON endpoint. Both legacy Go and native plumbing plans use this path; issue plans and modeled proposals keep their existing views. Use the complete saved proposal as authority and verify its plan hash before publishing source data. Stripping the state projection must never mutate the saved plan, its source map, its hash or the marker used for ratification.

Use the same on-demand source view on the public page and /act. Opening a proposal's acceptance-source disclosure fetches that hash's sources, displays loading/failure/retry states, and renders the exact text with the existing literal escaping and language highlighting. Closed disclosures and ordinary state polls must not fetch source bodies. Deduplicate concurrent requests and reuse successful responses by full hash, preserving open source views across ordinary refreshes. If a proposal changes while a request is pending, its old response must never populate the replacement proposal. Failed requests remain retryable; a missing source response must not be presented as an empty or successful review.

Serve only known proposal payloads through validated full-hash URLs, with the dashboard's existing GET/HEAD-only public access policy and security headers; unknown or malformed hashes and unavailable sources get a non-success response. Do not accept filesystem paths, issue numbers or shortened hashes as source authority. Retain exact bytes such as CRLF and a missing final newline. A successful source URL must never return a different proposal's bytes after refresh or restart. Sources can be cached separately by hash; any persisted payload must be checked against its hash before use. Preserve restart behavior so a saved state can show its matching saved sources while GitHub is unavailable, or an explicit unavailable state if that source cache is missing/corrupt. An older cached state containing inline sources must be migrated to the lightweight projection or discarded for refresh, never served verbatim and never attached to an unverified hash.

Read internal/dashboard/{issues.go,dashboard.go,http.go,acted.go,previews.go} and web/app.js for state publication, cached restart, authenticated state, and shared proposal rendering. Existing tests to inspect include native_identity_view_accept_test.go, dashboard_test.go, act_test.go, ratifyall_accept_test.go, acted_accept_test.go and the preview-cache tests. TestNativeProposalViewRetainsFullIdentityAndSource currently pins inline sources in the waiting view: intentionally replace that expectation with retained identities in state and exact source retrieval through the full-hash endpoint. Name internal/dashboard/native_identity_view_accept_test.go in the child plan's files and state that change in its summary, along with every other existing test requiring edits. Keep command authorization, ratification hashes and confirmations unchanged.

Acceptance and regression tests must cover small polled state with multiple large sources, exact hash-addressed retrieval for legacy and native plans, no mutation of stored proposals, full-hash isolation, unknown/malformed hashes, method restrictions, source-cache restart/corruption, and both page consumers. Use Go acceptance tests in the owning dashboard package for HTTP and state behavior, and the existing embedded-asset test conventions for both pages' wiring, without adding external dependencies. Verify the browser interaction with controlled responses: no eager or repeated poll downloads, one fetch for repeated opens, literal rendering, retry, and a stale response after proposal replacement; document the reproducible browser check if no existing browser harness is available. Run dashboard tests, including public and /act command tests.

Update docs/factory.md and the corresponding native-proposal/dashboard statements in SPEC.md to explain that full identities remain in state and verbatim source is loaded on opening by full proposal hash. Detail belongs in docs/factory.md, linked by the README, rather than expanding the front page. Cite D-0314 and applicable dashboard decisions D-0051/D-0060/D-0065, with D-0122/D-0294 for current-state documentation. This work also rests on D-0107 (ratification identity), D-0317 (intentional pinned-test changes) and D-0105 (tested plumbing). The merger records the new source-delivery/cache decision; the build cannot write decisions/.
